title: Sanctification
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Sanctification is God’s work of making believers holy and conforming them increasingly to the likeness of Jesus Christ. It is a grace-driven process involving the Word, the Spirit, faith, repentance, obedience, and endurance.
summary: Sanctification is God’s work of making believers holy and conforming them increasingly to the likeness of Jesus Christ. It is a grace-driven process involving the Word, the Spirit, faith, repentance, obedience, and endurance.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is both the ground and goal of sanctification. Believers are made holy in Him and are being formed to reflect His character, love, purity, humility, and obedience.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sanctification means God does not leave His people unchanged. Those whom He saves, He begins to make holy. Salvation includes forgiveness and transformation.

The believer’s growth in holiness is God’s work, yet believers are called to active obedience. Scripture holds together God’s power and the believer’s responsibility to pursue holiness.

The Word and Spirit are central to sanctification. God sanctifies His people by truth, renews their minds, convicts them of sin, and forms Christlike character over time.

Sanctification is often slow, painful, and ordinary. It includes repentance, suffering, discipline, obedience, community, prayer, and perseverance. God uses these means to make His people more like Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people either expect instant perfection or settle for no change at all. Sanctification rejects both despair and passivity. God is patient with His people, but He is also committed to their holiness.

This doctrine is essential for recovery and discipleship because freedom is not merely escaping consequences. True restoration includes being formed into the likeness of Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pursue holiness by grace. Do not try to sanctify yourself by fleshly striving, and do not excuse sin as though change is impossible. Stay in the Word, depend on the Spirit, repent quickly, obey faithfully, and trust God to continue shaping you into Christ’s likeness.
